format: single Home Instead franchised business (non-medical home care office serving a Protected Area of about 10,000 people aged 65+)

invest.quote: The total investment necessary to begin operation of a Home Instead® franchised business is $92,640–$350,550. This includes $54,000–$56,250 which must be paid to us as the initial franchise fee.

fee.quote: You must pay us an initial franchise fee of $54,000 ("Initial Franchise Fee"). The Initial Franchise Fee is due when you sign the Franchise Agreement.
fee.note: VetFran: 20% discount (fee reduced to $43,200) for honorably discharged U.S. veterans who do not already own a Home Instead franchise. Optional $27,000 Deposit Agreement to reserve a market ($24,300 refundable if withdrawn within 90 days). Fee covers training for two people; Additional Trainee Fee $2,250 per person (max $2,700). During 2025 franchisees paid $0 to $54,000.

royalty.quote: Royalty Fee 5% of Gross Sales 15th and the last day of each month or such other dates as specified in the Operations Manual

adFund.quote: Marketing Fund 2% of monthly Gross Sales ... You must contribute 2% of monthly Gross Sales to the Fund (as defined in Item 11).

otherRecurring.name: Technology Fee
otherRecurring.amount: Our then-current fee (currently $500/month); may not increase more than 25% per calendar year

otherRecurring.name: Fees for Required Systems
otherRecurring.amount: currently ranges from $177 to $1,861 per month for systems billed on a recurring monthly basis, and up to $3,457 in any month in which annual system fees are billed

otherRecurring.name: Bulk Purchasing Administrative Fee
otherRecurring.amount: Up to 10% of the cost for any Required System or optional system or other product or service where we have arranged for a network contract

transferFee.amount: $25,000 Payable by either the transferee or transferor at the time ownership of the franchise is transferred. (Minority Ownership Change Fee $9,000)

item19.note: Gross Sales only; 'The Gross Sales data in the tables above do not contain any information regarding the cost of sales, operating expenses, or other costs or expenses'. Excludes affiliate-owned businesses, 15 franchises opened after January 1, 2025, closed and 4 terminated locations. By territory tenure, 31.6% of the 611 businesses have 21-25 years and 35.7% have 26+ years; 14 have 1-2 years.

special: Home care is labor-intensive: Gross Sales are billings for caregiver hours and Item 19 shows no costs. The franchisor is owned by Honor Technology, Inc.; some existing franchisees operate under Honor's 'Care Platform' (Honor or its affiliates recruit and employ caregivers, manage care and bill clients), paid to Honor. Institutional owners may have to post an escrow or letter of credit equal to 3% of prior 12-month gross revenue (or up to $65,000 for a greenfield).
issues: Item 19 average and median carry cents ($2,750,875.94; $2,352,450.95), truncated to whole dollars. Pending franchisee lawsuits over early renewal rights under a March 2024 settlement (Item 3).
